title: Is arbitration in India finally moving toward online dispute resolution
p1:
A dispute that once required packed files, conference rooms, and months of travel can now begin with a few clicks.

But is India really ready for online arbitration, or is it just a digital version of the old system?
p2: Many people think arbitration always means sitting before a panel in a physical hearing room. The surprising reality is that technology is changing how disputes are managed — from filing documents online to conducting virtual hearings and using digital platforms for communication.
p3:
Online dispute resolution does not simply mean replacing a courtroom with a video call. It aims to make dispute resolution faster, more accessible, and less expensive, especially for businesses and individuals who cannot afford long legal processes.

The practical takeaway: the future of arbitration may depend not only on legal rules, but also on trust in secure digital systems and fair online procedures.
conclusion: Do you think online arbitration can make justice faster in India, or will people still prefer traditional hearings?
